title: Onboarding Immersion & Rotation Program: Guide for Managers and People Ops
author: Priya K. Shah
content:
Summary

This guide defines Redwood's Onboarding Immersion & Rotation Program (OIRP), a structured 6–12 month path for new hires that pairs deep role onboarding with short cross-functional rotations. OIRP aims to accelerate time-to-impact, broaden institutional knowledge, and create stronger manager/peer relationships while preserving recruiting velocity and role clarity.

Goals

- Reduce meaningful ramp time to first independent production contribution to <= 60 days for ICs and <= 90 days for managers.
- Provide at least one cross-functional rotation (2–6 weeks) during the first 6 months for applicable hires.
- Maintain clarity of role expectations and promotion readiness through checkpointed feedback.
- Equip managers with repeatable checklists and decision criteria to approve, monitor, and conclude rotations.

Scope and Applicability

- Applies to most full-time technical and product hires (IC and manager levels L3–L6).
- Not mandatory for contractor/temporary roles, some highly specialized roles (e.g., kernel optimization engineers requiring continuous focus), or customer-facing roles with strict ramp constraints—exceptions require People Ops sign-off.

Program Overview

1) Immersion (Weeks 0–6) — Role-first onboarding
   - Week 0: Preboarding tasks (credentials, workspace, docs).
   - Week 1: Orientation and core systems overview (Redwood API, internal infra, security basics).
   - Weeks 2–6: Deep role-specific onboarding: shadowing, small deliverables, playbook review, and initial pairing.

2) Rotation (Weeks 7–18) — Short cross-functional experience
   - Typical rotation length: 2–6 weeks (agreement at hire or by week 4).
   - Rotation partners: adjacent teams (e.g., infra ⇄ serving runtime, product ⇄ developer experience, SRE ⇄ infra capacity).
   - Outcomes: concrete learning goals, one short deliverable (doc, mini-feature, triage report), and presentation to sponsors.

3) Re-integration & Calibration (Weeks 19–26) — Apply learning to primary role
   - Integrate knowledge into regular roadmap work.
   - Checkpoints and performance calibration with manager and People Ops.

Roles & Responsibilities

- New Hire:
  - Own learning goals, deliver rotation tasks, present rotation readout.
  - Seek feedback at scheduled checkpoints.

- Hiring Manager (Primary Manager):
  - Define role-specific immersion curriculum before start (tasks, docs, pairing plan).
  - Approve rotation scope by week 4 and identify rotation sponsor.
  - Conduct checkpoints at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 26; sign off re-integration plan.

- Rotation Sponsor (Receiving Team Manager):
  - Specify concrete work and mentorship, provide onboarding for their domain.
  - Give timely feedback using rotation rubric.

- Buddy / Peer Mentor:
  - Day-to-day touchpoint for the first 90 days.
  - Responsible for contextual help (channel orientation, codebase paths, meeting norms).

- People Ops:
  - Maintain program materials, approve exceptions, collect program-wide metrics, and coordinate manager training.

Decision Criteria for Rotations

Managers should confirm the following before approving a rotation:

- Role-critical milestones for the primary role are defined and not jeopardized (list attached).
- Rotation work has a clear, time-boxed scope and a concrete deliverable.
- Rotation sponsor has available mentorship bandwidth (>= 2 hours/week confirmed).
- New hire has completed critical security and compliance training required for rotation domain.

Rotation Rubric (sample)

- Scope Definition: Clear goals and deliverable (Pass / Needs revision).
- Mentorship Availability: Sponsor commits >= 2 weekly touchpoints (Yes / No).
- Knowledge Transferability: Skill gained maps to primary role (High/Medium/Low).
- Impact: Rotation deliverable has measurable outcome (e.g., doc, small PR, incident triage).

Program Timeline: Example (IC Engineer)

| Phase | Duration | Key Activities | Checkpoint | Deliverable |
|-------|----------|----------------|------------|-------------|
| Preboard | -7 to -1 days | Access, invite to #new-hires, setup laptop | Preboard checklist complete | Account access list |
| Immersion | 0–6 weeks | Orientation, codebase tours, small bug fix | Week 4 manager 1:1 | 2 small PRs or a docs contribution |
| Rotation | 7–18 weeks | 2–6 week rotation, attend team rituals | Rotation end review | Rotation readout doc + demo |
| Re-integrate | 19–26 weeks | Apply learnings, roadmap alignment | Week 26 calibration | Contribution plan for next 6 months |

Manager Checklist (pre-hire and first 8 weeks)

Pre-hire:
1. Create a role activation packet: onboarding tasks, list of code owners, 90-day success criteria.
2. Identify potential buddies and rotation sponsors.
3. Confirm on-call/critical rotation blackout windows; adjust start date if needed.

Week 0–2:
1. Run orientation and team intro schedule.
2. Assign buddy and set 3-day, 2-week, and 6-week goals.
3. Ensure first tickets and pairing sessions are available.

Week 3–8:
1. Revisit goals in week 4 checkpoint; sign rotation approval by week 4 if applicable.
2. Provide direct feedback after first PRs and pairing.
3. Confirm budgeted mentorship time with rotation sponsor.

Performance & Feedback Integration

- Checkpoints are explicit feedback moments—not just status updates. Use the following template during checkpoints:
  - Context: What was assigned and why.
  - Observations: Specific behaviors and outputs.
  - Impact: How this affects team/customer outcomes.
  - Next steps: Concrete, time-bound actions.

- Use calibrated rubrics aligned to Redwood’s performance framework (contributor impact, craftsmanship, collaboration, ownership). Link templates: /confluence/people-ops/feedback-templates.

- If a new hire is underperforming at any checkpoint, follow the Performance Improvement Flow (PIF) — see section below. Escalate to People Ops if not resolved after 2 checkpoints.

Performance Improvement Flow (PIF) — condensed steps

1. Manager documents gap with examples and expected outcomes.
2. 2-week focused support plan with measurable milestones.
3. If progress insufficient, formal PIP initiated by People Ops with HR involvement.

Measurement & Success Metrics

People Ops will track program metrics quarterly: 
- Median time-to-first-merged-PR by cohort.
- Percentage of hires completing at least one rotation within first 6 months.
- Manager and new-hire satisfaction (post-90-day survey) target >= 85% favorable.
- 6-month retention rate for OIRP participants vs baseline.

Policy and Exceptions

- Security-sensitive rotations require explicit approval from Security team; completion of domain-specific compliance training is mandatory.
- Product/Customer-touch roles may have rotation windows restricted during commercial launch periods.
- Managers may defer rotations for up to 3 months if business-critical deliverables require full focus; People Ops should be notified and rationale recorded.

Sample Rotation Request Template (to be emailed to People Ops and sponsor)

Subject: Rotation Request — [New Hire Name] — [Primary Team] → [Sponsor Team] — Proposed Dates

Body:
- New hire & level: [Name, Title/Level]
- Primary manager: [Name]
- Proposed rotation dates: [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
- Rotation goals (3 bullets):
  1. …
  2. …
  3. …
- Deliverable: [Doc / PR / Triage report]
- Sponsor & mentor: [Name] (confirmed)
- Security/compliance notes: [training completed?]

FAQ

Q: Is rotation mandatory?
A: No. It is strongly encouraged for career development, but managers may opt out for business-critical reasons with People Ops approval.

Q: Will time in rotation count as time in primary role for compensation/promotion?
A: Yes. Rotation time counts as role tenure and is considered in promotion calibration when accompanied by documented deliverables and manager assessments.

Q: What if the rotation sponsor’s team is overloaded?
A: Sponsors must confirm at least 2 hours/week mentorship. If unavailable, consider a lighter shadowing rotation or delay.

Appendix: Example 4-week Rotation Syllabus (Frontend Engineer → DevEx)

Week 1: Orientation to DevEx priorities, observe onboarding flows, reading list.
Week 2: Pair on a small instrumenting task (metrics hook), create a spike.
Week 3: Own a small improvement and open PR, start a 15-min demo doc.
Week 4: Finalize deliverable, present readout to both teams, document handoff notes.

Ownership & Revision Cycle

People Ops owns this guide and the OIRP program; teams should treat it as a living document. Major changes must be reviewed by two People Ops leads and one engineering manager stakeholder. Annual review scheduled for Q4 each year.
